description: Apium graveolens var. dulce: grown for its thick leaf stalks.

diseases.name: Anthracnose (Leaf Curl)
diseases.description: A fungal disease that curls celery leaves and cracks the leaf stalks.
diseases.causes: Spores spread by rain splash and overhead irrigation in warm, wet weather; they come in on transplants and weeds.
symptoms: Brown, sunken lesions on leaf stalks, which crack
diseases.untreated: Whole plantings can be lost in warm, wet summers.

steps.title: Remove curled, cracked plants
steps.instruction: Pick off curled, cracked plants when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores come in on transplants and weeds.
Splash carries them across the crop.
Leaves curl; stalks get sunken lesions.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: celery anthracnose

diseases.name: Early Blight
diseases.description: Cercospora early blight: a fungal leaf spot of celery in warm, humid weather.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on debris and seed and spread by wind and splash; warm, humid weather with dew favours it.
symptoms: Small yellow spots that grow into tan to grey lesions
Lesions angular, with a grey bloom of spores in humid weather
Lesions merge and leaflets die; stalks can be spotted
diseases.effect: Spotted leaves and stalks lower quality and yield.

steps.title: Remove spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Water in the morning, at the base
Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on debris and seed.
